title: Foundations of Writing
full_title: Foundations of Writing: Observation, Narrative and Description
tagline: The writing process, observation and material, theme and structure, narration, description, expressing feeling, exposition, language and punctuation, and revision
summary: Most school leavers have written hundreds of compositions to a formula; good writing starts from looking closely and saying exactly what you mean. This course covers the writing process from observation and gathering material to choosing a theme and a structure, the modes of narration, description, expression of feeling and exposition, clear and correct language including punctuation, and the habit of revision.

chapters.title: The writing process
chapters.summary: From the urge to write to a finished piece: gathering, planning, drafting and revising, and why formulaic exam compositions are a poor model.

chapters.title: Observation and material
chapters.summary: Seeing and recording precisely, keeping notebooks, reading as a writer, and choosing material.

chapters.title: Theme and structure
chapters.summary: Finding what a piece is about, openings and endings, transitions and echoes, and the shape of the whole.

chapters.title: Narration
chapters.summary: Telling events clearly: order, person and point of view, pace, and detail.

chapters.title: Description
chapters.summary: Describing people, places and scenes through the senses, and the difference between description and decoration.

chapters.title: Expressing feeling
chapters.summary: Direct and indirect expression of feeling, feeling conveyed through scene and event, and restraint.

chapters.title: Exposition
chapters.summary: Explaining things and processes clearly: definition, classification, example, comparison and figures.

chapters.title: Language and punctuation
chapters.summary: Plain, precise language, the national standards for punctuation (GB/T 15834—2011) and for numbers (GB/T 15835—2011), and common errors.

chapters.title: Revision
chapters.summary: Revising for content, structure and language, reading aloud to check, and giving and using feedback.
